_note: The gauntlet twin: an INDEPENDENTLY-trained population on the same roster and the same run mechanics as run_default.json, diverging purely from a different nondeterministic training trajectory. That is the whole design -- a shared, population-wide blind spot is something an independently-evolved population exposes and a deck's own history never can. Everything below is what genuinely differs from run_default.json (league_name, and gauntlet_league_name pointing BACK at it so the twin reports vs_gauntlet against the main league from its first session); mechanics, roster, total_games, and heuristic_decks are inherited via "extends" -- they used to be retyped here and had silently drifted once already (games_per_iteration and pfsp_power were absent, so this trained at 6 games/iteration against the main league's 24), which is exactly the kind of difference that makes a twin comparison measure the config instead of the training; extends makes that drift structurally impossible now instead of relying on a test to catch it. The confound that disabled the ORIGINAL gauntlet is now structurally impossible for an unrelated reason too: it was trained against a frozen shared stack that was later deleted, and its weights were then loaded onto the calling population's unrelated embedding space -- silently invalid, not a crash. Per-deck encoders (2026-08-17) put the encoder inside each checkpoint, so a population can only ever be played through the perception it was trained with, and the stack_id.txt guard that policed this is gone.
